terra.problem: Calling Joash's rescue a good deal and joking that he didn't get a vote makes light of the danger surrounding the murders.
The explanation repeats that the nurse, not the mother, was in the room without adding anything; it sounds flat and generic.
The passage does not say nobody thought to look there or that the hiding place was in front of everybody.
It claims Joash would be found quickly in a palace, which the text does not establish.
Saying the secret comes out into the open suggests public disclosure, but Jehoiada shows Joash to the commanders under oath.
The statement that this is happening in Judah is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The interview-process joke makes light of the order to put people to death.
The joke about a polite escort home makes light of the order to put people to death.
The claim that the bodyguard never takes a break goes beyond the order and overlooks the divisions coming on and going off duty.
The passage says the weapons came from the house of the LORD, not a back room.
The passage identifies the spears and shields as David's; it does not say his name was written on them.
Saying the weapons come straight from David suggests he handed them over, but the passage says Jehoiada gave them to the commanders.
The explanation repeats that the item is a crown in three short ways without adding anything distinctive.
The passage does not say Athaliah believed Joash was dead or did not know he was alive.
The officers and trumpeters are beside the king, but the text does not say the people are all around him.
Identifying Joash as king of Judah uses a fact from outside the passage without a reference.
Apart from the quotation, the explanation repeats that Athaliah did not say murder and sounds flat.
The claim that not a single thing was left standing goes beyond the temple being torn down and its altars and idols smashed.
Saying lampstands stayed out of it asserts what happened to them; the passage simply does not mention them.
The explanation repeats the answer without adding a distinct observation or Papa Dorin's voice.
The passage does not mention a chariot, but it does not say there was no chariot in sight.
The joke about the young king being tiny and his feet not reaching the floor targets his age and size.
